fields.title: Fix the shard id as a 16-bit integer
fields.decision: Every shard id is a `short` (Int16 / SMALLINT). The shard id type is not a generic parameter anywhere: not on shard keys, shard sets, batches or result handlers.
fields.context: Early versions made the shard id type generic, so it could be a byte, int, string or Guid. Within any one application that type can never vary, yet every declaration in the object model and in consuming code had to restate it. The type also determines storage cost wherever a shard-qualified foreign key is persisted.

alternatives.whyRejected: It produced a verbose, redundant object model (`ShardSets<short>`, `ShardKey<short, int>`, `ShardBatch<short, …>`) for flexibility no application could use, since the type is fixed per application.
Smaller, but 255 shards is a plausible ceiling for global or tenant-per-database deployments.

alternatives.option: Fix it as `int` or a Guid.
alternatives.whyRejected: Doubles or octuples the storage of every persisted shard reference, for a shard count no deployment will approach.

fields.consequences: Simpler APIs (`ShardKey<TRecord>`), a compact two-byte shard component in every serialized key, and a theoretical ceiling of tens of thousands of shards. Older documentation and samples that show a shard type parameter (`ShardKey<byte, int>`, `ShardBatch<short, …>`) are obsolete.
